Deep Residual Network (ResNet)
Ellipsis counters: stage 2 repeats 24× · stage 3 repeats 36×
Stage 1 bottleneck
Conv 1×1: 256→64 · Conv 3×3: 64→64 · Conv 1×1: 64→256
Guided tour
1. Tensor pipeline
Click a stage slab for its bottleneck channel counts; click a BN / ReLU / Conv box in the inset for what it does.
The dotted ellipsis in each bracket means “this slab pattern repeats”.
Drag the figure to ease the oblique shear out and reveal the true 3-D slabs; “Figure view” restores the printed projection.

plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the architecture of a deep residual network (ResNet) at two levels of detail. The main diagram traces the flow of feature tensors through successive stages of the network, with labeled spatial and channel dimensions at each stage: a 7x7 convolution produces 112x112x64 feature maps, which are then processed through four residual stages yielding progressively smaller but deeper tensors — 56x56x256, 28x28x512, 14x14x1024, and 7x7x2048 — before a final average pooling and fully connected (AvgPool + FC) layer. Between stages, Subsample blocks reduce spatial resolution while increasing channel depth; within each stage, repeated ResBlocks (indicated by ellipses and annotations such as '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total') apply the same transformation many times. An inset zooms into the internal structure of a single ResBlock, showing the sequence: Conv 1x1 (bottleneck squeeze), Batch Normalization (BN), ReLU, Conv 3x3 (spatial convolution), BN, ReLU, and Conv 1x1 (channel expansion), with a skip connection bypassing these layers and adding the input directly to the output. The figure introduces the residual (skip-connection) design that allows very deep networks to be trained effectively by ensuring gradients can flow directly from later to earlier layers.

elements: Input image plane drawn as a thin slab (224 × 224 × 3) at far left, photo texture of candles on dark background, leaning parallelogram face
Diagonal leader line + rotated label '224 × 224 × 3' pointing to the image plane
Orange slab immediately right of the image = first conv output 112 × 112 × 64
Rotated label '112 × 112 × 64' with leader line to the orange slab
Stage-1 group: four blue-gray ResBlock slabs (56 × 56 × 256, bottleneck 64) bottom-aligned on the baseline, first three tightly packed, fourth slightly separated
Stage-2 group: two blue-gray slabs (28 × 28 × 512, bottleneck 128), a near-cube then a wider slab
Stage-3 group: one-to-two blue-gray slabs (14 × 14 × 1024, bottleneck 256)
Stage-4 group: three long blue-gray slabs (7 × 7 × 2048, bottleneck 512)
Two pale-teal thin vertical bars at far right, each labeled '1000', with dotted ellipsis mid-bar (FC logits and softmax output)
Bracket/pointer arrows above each stage carrying rotated labels 'ResBlock 56 × 56 × 256(64)', 'ResBlock 28 × 28 × 512(128)', 'ResBlock 14 × 14 × 1024(256)', 'ResBlock 7 × 7 × 2048(512)'
Dotted ellipsis with two dots and annotations '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total' between stage groups
Bottom-left diagonal arrows with labels 'Conv 7×7 Stride 2' and 'MaxPool'
Three bottom diagonal arrows labeled 'Subsample' pointing at the first block of stages 2, 3 and 4
Bottom-right diagonal arrows labeled 'AvgPool + FC' and 'Softmax' pointing to the two 1000-vectors
Inset panel: rounded gray rectangle at top right
Inset: single blue-gray cube on the left of the panel, an '=' sign, then the expanded chain
Inset chain boxes in order: BN (orange), ReLU (teal), Conv 1×1, BN (orange), ReLU (teal), Conv 3×3, BN (orange), ReLU (teal), Conv 1×1
Inset: black arrows connecting the chain boxes left to right
Inset: skip-connection arrow leaving the input node, running along the top of the panel, and descending into the ⊕ circle at the right end
Inset: ⊕ (circled plus) element-wise addition node and output arrow leaving the panel

interactions.teaches: that the whole network is just one ResBlock motif repeated, and that zooming in swaps the abstract cube for its internal BN–ReLU–Conv chain
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: that every stage runs the same bottleneck pattern, only the channel numbers change: Conv 1×1 squeezes to the bottleneck width (64/128/256/512), Conv 3×3 works at that width, Conv 1×1 expands to the stage output (256/512/1024/2048)
interactions.teaches_note: clicking any stage slab opens the ResBlock detail annotated with that stage's channel counts

interactions.teaches: that the input travels two routes at once — through BN/ReLU/Conv 1×1 → 3×3 → 1×1 and straight along the identity skip — and the two are summed element-wise at ⊕, so the block only has to learn a residual
interactions.label: Trace signal through ResBlock

interactions.teaches: that network depth changes only how many times the block is repeated per stage — the tensor shapes 112×112×64 … 7×7×2048 are fixed by the subsampling schedule, not by depth
interactions.label: Blocks total (network depth)

demo_steps.title: Tensor pipeline
demo_steps.narration: Follow the tensors left to right: the 224×224×3 image becomes 112×112×64 after Conv 7×7 stride 2, then four residual stages shrink space and grow channels to 7×7×2048 before AvgPool + FC gives 1000 logits.

demo_steps.title: Depth is repetition
demo_steps.narration: Push the depth slider to 36 blocks: more slabs appear inside each stage and the '36 blocks total' label updates, but every tensor dimension stays exactly the same.

demo_steps.title: Inside one block
demo_steps.narration: Open the inset: the single cube expands into BN → ReLU → Conv 1×1 → BN → ReLU → Conv 3×3 → BN → ReLU → Conv 1×1, with a skip line arcing over the top.

demo_steps.title: Two paths, one sum
demo_steps.narration: Play the signal trace: the main path is processed layer by layer while the identity copy runs unchanged along the skip; the ⊕ adds them, so gradients reach earlier layers directly.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Oblique projection: +X is screen-right and carries CHANNEL COUNT, +Y is screen-up and carries spatial HEIGHT, +Z is the receding diagonal (up-right, ~35°, 0.5 foreshortening) and carries spatial WIDTH. All slabs are bottom-aligned on a common baseline y=0 and laid out left to right along +X. Explicit sizes (X × Y × Z world units): input image 0.08 × 3.0 × 3.0 (photo texture, dark with orange candle flames); first conv slab 0.50 × 1.60 × 1.60 in orange #C4693B (front face) with darker side #9C4E2B; stage-1 ResBlocks 0.55 × 0.90 × 0.90 each (×4 drawn, small 0.08 gaps, 4th separated by 0.35); stage-2 ResBlocks 0.80 × 0.55 × 0.55 (×2); stage-3 ResBlocks 1.30 × 0.34 × 0.34 (×2); stage-4 ResBlocks 2.20 × 0.20 × 0.20 (×3, long horizontal bars); total span ≈ 18 units wide, 3 units tall. Final two logit bars: 0.12 × 1.30 × 0.12, pale teal #B6DFDA, separated by 0.35, each with a dotted ellipsis at mid-height and '1000' above. Palette: block front faces #A8BFCE, top faces #C6D6DF, right/side faces #5F7E8F, outlines black 1px; inset panel fill #BFBFBF with 0.15 rounded corners and black border; BN boxes #E2804F, ReLU boxes #A6DCD2, Conv boxes white #FFFFFF, all with black outlines and black connector arrows. Dimension labels ('224 × 224 × 3', '112 × 112 × 64', 'ResBlock 56 × 56 × 256(64)', etc.) are rotated about −33° matching the receding diagonal and sit above-left of their target with a thin leader arrow; 'Subsample', 'Conv 7×7 Stride 2', 'MaxPool', 'AvgPool + FC', 'Softmax' are rotated about −33° below the baseline with arrows pointing up-right into the first block of each stage. 'n blocks total' labels sit on the baseline between stage groups flanked by two dots and a dotted ellipsis. Inset occupies the upper-right quadrant, roughly 9 × 2 units, horizontally centered over stages 2–4. Bottleneck channel rule shown on click: Conv1×1 out = C/4, Conv3×3 = C/4, Conv1×1 out = C where C ∈ {256, 512, 1024, 2048}.
interactionPlan.notes: Render slabs as BoxGeometry with flat MeshBasicMaterial per-face shading (light top, mid front, dark right) plus black EdgesGeometry LineSegments for the hand-drawn outline look; use an OrthographicCamera with a sheared projection matrix (shear Z into X and Y by cos35°/sin35° × 0.5) rather than rotating the camera, so all front faces stay true rectangles. Image plane uses a CanvasTexture of the candle photo on the front face only. All text (dimension labels, 'Subsample', inset box captions) as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays so rotation and crispness are easy; arrows as Line + small cone meshes in the same overlay plane. Inset panel drawn as a separate orthographic HTML/SVG layer pinned to the top-right so it stays legible regardless of the 3D layout. Depth slider should add/remove slab meshes with a short scale-in tween and re-flow the layout along +X, keeping every slab's X/Y/Z size constant. Signal-flow animation: an emissive pulse sprite travelling the polyline through the inset chain and a second pulse on the skip polyline at matched speed, converging on the ⊕ which flashes and emits the output pulse; highlight each chain box as the pulse enters it. Clicking a stage slab dispatches a raycast hit that sets viewMode='ResBlock detail' and rewrites the inset channel captions (e.g. 'Conv 1×1: 256→64', 'Conv 3×3: 64→64', 'Conv 1×1: 64→256').

Guided tour
1. Tensor pipeline
Click any stage slab in the figure for its bottleneck channel counts.

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Inset ResBlock panel is drawn far too small relative to the source (where it dominates the upper-right); its chain labels (BN / ReLU / Conv 1×1) overflow their boxes and collide with neighbouring boxes, so the detail panel is unreadable in the default 'Full network' view.

Dimension leader labels are crowded: '224 × 224 × 3', '112 × 112 × 64' and 'ResBlock 56 × 56 × 256(64)' pile onto each other near the input, whereas the source spreads them along well-separated diagonal leaders.
The two '1000' logit-bar labels overlap into a single '100000' string; in the source they are clearly separated above each teal bar.

The stage bracket leaders are rendered as plain diagonal lines from a far z-plane rather than the source's flat horizontal bracket with short down-arrows onto each block, making the grouping relationship harder to read.
'24 blocks total' text sits directly on top of the slabs instead of in the empty gap between stages with the two flanking dots and dashed ellipsis, as in the source.
Input image slab is rendered with a synthetic gradient/candle canvas that only loosely resembles the source photo, and the black photo plane reads darker/flatter than the original.
evaluation.notes: Composition, oblique projection, stage progression and colour scheme closely reproduce the ResNet figure and the interaction set (view toggle, depth slider, signal trace, clickable slabs, guided tour) is rich and pedagogically apt, but the inset ResBlock panel is far too small with overflowing text and several dimension/logit labels collide, hurting legibility.

feedback.rationale: The concept, decomposition, and interaction set are correct (concept 5); the issues are execution-level rendering problems—undersized inset panel, overflowing/colliding labels, and leader-line styling—that call for implementation fixes rather than a new plan.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the architecture of a deep residual network (ResNet) at two levels of detail. The main diagram traces the flow of feature tensors through successive stages of the network, with labeled spatial and channel dimensions at each stage: a 7x7 convolution produces 112x112x64 feature maps, which are then processed through four residual stages yielding progressively smaller but deeper tensors — 56x56x256, 28x28x512, 14x14x1024, and 7x7x2048 — before a final average pooling and fully connected (AvgPool + FC) layer. Between stages, Subsample blocks reduce spatial resolution while increasing channel depth; within each stage, repeated ResBlocks (indicated by ellipses and annotations such as '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total') apply the same transformation many times. An inset zooms into the internal structure of a single ResBlock, showing the sequence: Conv 1x1 (bottleneck squeeze), Batch Normalization (BN), ReLU, Conv 3x3 (spatial convolution), BN, ReLU, and Conv 1x1 (channel expansion), with a skip connection bypassing these layers and adding the input directly to the output. The figure introduces the residual (skip-connection) design that allows very deep networks to be trained effectively by ensuring gradients can flow directly from later to earlier layers.

interactions.teaches: that the whole network is just one ResBlock motif repeated, and that zooming in swaps the abstract cube for its internal BN–ReLU–Conv chain
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: that every stage runs the same bottleneck pattern, only the channel numbers change: Conv 1×1 squeezes to the bottleneck width (64/128/256/512), Conv 3×3 works at that width, Conv 1×1 expands to the stage output (256/512/1024/2048)
interactions.teaches_note: clicking any stage slab opens the ResBlock detail annotated with that stage's channel counts

interactions.teaches: that the input travels two routes at once — through BN/ReLU/Conv 1×1 → 3×3 → 1×1 and straight along the identity skip — and the two are summed element-wise at ⊕, so the block only has to learn a residual
interactions.label: Trace signal through ResBlock

interactions.teaches: that network depth changes only how many times the block is repeated per stage — the tensor shapes 112×112×64 … 7×7×2048 are fixed by the subsampling schedule, not by depth
interactions.label: Blocks total (network depth)
